stated: Fully review and reform the Child Maintenance Service to ensure it works for all children and parents, including removing the Collect and Pay charge for receiving parents and ensuring that payments cannot be used as a form of coercive control over domestic abuse survivors.

source.quote: Fully review and reform the Child Maintenance Service to ensure it works for all children and parents, including removing the Collect and Pay charge for receiving parents and ensuring that payments cannot be used as a form of coercive control over domestic abuse survivors.

bearing_set.reason: Removing the 4% Collect and Pay charge for receiving parents directly increases disposable income for typically lower-income single-parent households relying on maintenance to cover essentials.
Reforming CMS to prevent payments being weaponised as coercive control directly addresses a known mechanism of domestic abuse — a safety and crime-prevention matter squarely within O5.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: a financial relief effect on cost of essentials (O2) and a crime/justice protection effect for domestic abuse survivors (O5). No material bearing on O11 (this is not a tax measure), O9 (the coercive control fix is a safety/justice matter rather than an anti-discrimination one), or O14 (the income gain is real but too narrow to move aggregate inequality indicators).
